data.title: Triamcinolone acetonide (cream, lotion, paste)
data.summary: IV Topical corticosteroids · Medium-potency fluorinated steroid (0.1% cream/lotion US class 5; ointment class 4)
data.body:
_Topicals · IV Topical corticosteroids_

**Class:** Medium-potency fluorinated steroid (0.1% cream/lotion US class 5; ointment class 4)

## Mechanism of action
- Glucocorticoid receptor agonist (acetonide group)

## Indications in dermatology & STI
- Cream/lotion 0.1%: eczema, psoriasis, lichen planus, insect bite reactions, body and scalp (lotion)
- Dental/oral paste 0.1% (in Orabase — adheres to wet mucosa): oral lichen planus, aphthous ulcers, mucous membrane pemphigoid and other erosive oral lesions
- Also used intralesionally (injectables slot)

## Dose & formulations
- Cream/lotion: 2–3 times daily (or once daily for maintenance)
- Oral paste: dab (do not rub) a small amount onto the dried lesion 2–4 times daily, preferably after meals and at bedtime

## Adverse effects
- Skin: as for medium-potency steroids
- Oral paste: oral candidiasis (thrush) with prolonged use — add an antifungal if needed

## Contraindications
- Skin infections; oral paste — oral herpes, candidiasis, untreated infection

## Pregnancy & lactation
Acceptable on limited areas.

## Viva points
- Orabase paste sticks to wet mucosa — main topical steroid for oral lesions
- Watch for oral candidiasis

_Sources: Wolverton 4e ch.45 and ch.61 (Oral mucosal therapeutics); Khopkar ch.22. Facts summarised in our own words; Wolverton followed where books differ._
